GT_reasoning: The system provides audit logs and access reports for review, but it does not implement security-incident tracking reports. It also doesn't enforce regular reviewing.

description: The system must ensure that the notice of privacy practices informs individuals of their right to inspect their protected health information.
LLM_reasoning: Notice mentions access/participation but not clearly the right to inspect
GT_reasoning: The Access/Participation section states: The privacy policy requires us to allow you access to your medical records, which partially addresses inspection and access.

description: The system must ensure that the notice of privacy practices informs individuals of their right to request an amendment to their protected health information.
LLM_reasoning: Notice doesn't state right to request amendment
GT_reasoning: The Access/Participation section states: Please contact the iTrust System Administrator or your medical professional if you feel any information is incorrect or needs to be changed, which implies a right to amendment but never explicitly frames it as a formal right.

description: The system shall support conducting an accurate and thorough assessment of potential risks and vulnerabilities to the integrity of electronic protected health information (ePHI)
LLM_reasoning: Audit trail provides traceability; but no explicit risk/vulnerability assessment process or integrity checking
GT_reasoning: The system does not implement any explicit risk assessment mechanism for assessing the integrity.

description: The system must ensure that each description of permitted or required use or disclosure includes sufficient detail to notify the individual of how their information may be used or disclosed.
LLM_reasoning: Privacy page lists permitted uses but is general, not tied to specific disclosures
GT_reasoning: The privacy policy contains no mention of how the information will be used or disclosed.

description: The system must ensure that the notice of privacy practices describes the types of uses and disclosures that require written authorization, includes a statement that any other uses or disclosures will only be made with written authorization, and informs the individual of their right to revoke that authorization.
LLM_reasoning: States written authorization needed outside listed uses but lacks detail on types and omits revocation rights
GT_reasoning: The policy only vaguely mentions written authorization for disclosures outside the listed permitted categories, but never describes the specific types of uses or disclosures that require it. There is also no mention of the individual's right to revoke authorization.
note: gt and llm say the same thing but llm rates it higher

description: The system shall not allow a covered entity to use or disclose protected health information without a valid authorization.
LLM_reasoning: System relies on role-based access; no capture/verification of patient authorizations. DeclareHCP provides visibility not enforcement
GT_reasoning: The functions that use or disclose health inforamtion can only be accessed and called by authorization

description: The system shall ensure that any use or disclosure of PHI does not exceed the scope defined in the authorization.
LLM_reasoning: No mechanism to store or enforce authorization scope beyond roles
GT_reasoning: , The functions that use or disclose health inforamtion are accessed based on their role which defines the scope of their authorization

description: The system shall protect against any reasonably anticipated threats or hazards to the security of electronic protected health information (ePHI).
LLM_reasoning: RBAC/logging/timeouts exist; legacy SHA-256 hashing without KDF/MFA; no TLS or at-rest encryption; no global rate limiting
GT_reasoning: The system protects against any reasonably anticipated threats or hazards to the security of ePHI by (1) Many JSPs use StringEscapeUtils.escapeHtml() when outputting user input to help guard against script injection in the browser. However, it is not enforced across the entire codebase. For example, Review text is user-generated, and output without escaping is a direct XSS risk.  Also, appointment comments are stored and displayed without escaping. (2) DAOs use PreparedStatement for database access, so user input is parameterized and not concatenated into SQL, reducing SQL injection risk. (3) Validators and ValidationFormat reject invalid input. (4) The only upload (patient CSV) is parsed as CSV, so the app does not blindly accept arbitrary files.

description: The system shall protect against any reasonably anticipated threats or hazards to the integrity of electronic protected health information (ePHI).
LLM_reasoning: Validators and DB constraints help; no tamper-evident storage/signing, integrity monitoring, or at-rest crypto
GT_reasoning: The system does not protect against any reasonably anticipated threats or hazards to the integrity of stored data (e.g. hashes or signatures on records) to detect tampering outside the application (e.g. direct DB changes). Integrity is only supported by access control and authorization, but not by cryptographic or storage-level integrity checks.

description: The system shall protect against any reasonably anticipated uses of electronic protected health information (ePHI) that are not permitted or required.
LLM_reasoning: RBAC only; no purpose-of-use capture, policy engine, or consistent minimum-necessary enforcement
GT_reasoning: The system protects against unpermitted uses of ePHI through authentication and role-based access control enforced in web.xml. All ePHI lives under /auth/*, and require a valid login, and access is further scoped by role and by patient-specific ownership checks

description: The system shall protect against any disclosures of electronic protected health information (ePHI) that are not permitted or required.
LLM_reasoning: Records release requires patient auth/signature; lacks masking, minimum-necessary export controls, TLS/at-rest encryption
GT_reasoning: The system protects against unpermitted disclosures of ePHI through authentication and role-based access control enforced in web.xml. All ePHI lives under /auth/*, and require a valid login, and access is further scoped by role and by patient-specific ownership checks

description: The system must ensure that individuals receive adequate notice of the covered entity’s legal duties regarding protected health information.
LLM_reasoning: Legal duties referenced generally; not versioned/acknowledged or change-notified
GT_reasoning: There is only one privacy policy in the code, and in it, there is no mention of covered entity’s legal duties regarding protected health information

description: The system shall ensure that any use, disclosure, or request of protected health information (PHI) is limited to the minimum amount necessary to accomplish the intended purpose.
LLM_reasoning: Only telemedicine metric flags; no systematic minimum-necessary enforcement or data minimization
GT_reasoning: The system does not consistently apply minimum necessary when retrieving PHI. Several flows load full patient records when only one or two fields are needed.

description: The system shall treat any disclosure of a code or mechanism that enables re-identification as a disclosure of protected health information (PHI).
LLM_reasoning: No de-identification/re-identification handling; PHI directly linked via MID; no protected mapping
GT_reasoning: There is no process of de-identifying information in the code

description: The system shall ensure the availability of all electronic protected health information (ePHI) that it creates.
LLM_reasoning: Data stored with audit log; availability depends on single MyISAM instance with no backup/HA
GT_reasoning: Created ePHI is written to the database, and once the transaction commits, it is available for later reads. The application does not implement backup or recovery of created data. So, in the event of database or storage loss or corruption, that data would be unavailable or lost.

description: The system shall ensure the availability of all electronic protected health information (ePHI) that it receives.
LLM_reasoning: Incoming ePHI stored in MyISAM tables; no replication/ACID/backup or disaster recovery
GT_reasoning: Transmission of ePHI only occurs when the user can load pages that include authenticate.jsp; that logic returns 503 when the database is unavailable, so the application does not attempt to transmit ePHI when it cannot reliably read or serve it.
